what_it_checks: that a served model outside the request's declared equivalence set, or any substitution on a request that forbids downgrading, is a typed failure
that refusing a request while some non-down provider still had request, token and concurrency headroom for a legally substitutable model is a typed failure
that dispatching into an announced outage more than the grace of 8 attempts loses the request
that a request is completed and billed exactly once
that every request ends either completed or refused: one left in neither state is a typed loss
that waiting more than 32 times on a request no provider could ever serve is treated as losing it, not as patience
that the router's copy of a request still matches harness truth after every callback
that a non-progressing policy aborts loudly against a 512-decision-per-request budget instead of grinding
that a bill is never negative and never below the all-cached price floor
that the provider's own meter and the harness's independent ledger agree at end of run
that the frozen fleet configuration is byte-identical at end of run: nothing the router touched aliased the fleet's own tables
that dispatching to an unknown provider or to a provider that does not stock the model is a typed failure and does NOT reschedule the request
that a refused, lost or dead request counts as SLO-violated in its tenant's rate, so dropping hard traffic cannot improve the rate
that a refused request books zero quality and a quality-floor miss
the trusted-correct oracle every kept test must pass: requested model, first provider that stocks it, wait otherwise
